Construct the mixture of two normal distributions for each signature

Source: R/internalFunctions.R
normalMix.Rd

This function constructs a comprehensive mixture of two normal distributions for each signature using the pooled sampled values from the up-scaling step.

Usage

normalMix(geneLists, resultNorm)

Arguments

geneLists

a list containing signature gene lists.

resultNorm

a list containing one entry for each gene signature present in the geneLists object. Each entry contains a matrix with all the values sampled from the normal distribution obtained from the GSVA score (mean) and the permutations (standard deviation). One row of the matrix represents one sample. The columns correspond to the number of draws.

Value

a list containing one entry for each gene signature present in the geneLists object. Each entry contains the mixtures of two normal distributions for the signature calculated with sampled values. The entry corresponds to the object returned by the `mixtools::normalmixEM` function. When the mixture of two normal distributions cannot be calculated successfully, the \'NA\' value is present.

Author

Astrid Deschênes

Examples


## Required library
library(GSVA)

## Load signatures
data(signaturesDemo)

## Create a list of two signatures
geneLists <- list()
geneLists[["classical"]] <- 
    signaturesDemo$`Classical`
geneLists[["basal"]] <- 
    signaturesDemo$`Basal-like`

## Load demo normalized expected counts
data(expNormalCountsDemo)

## Fix seed for reproducibility
set.seed(144)

## Calculate GSVA scores for the signatures
gsvaParameter <- gsvaParam(exprData=as.matrix(expNormalCountsDemo),
    geneSets=geneLists)
resClass <- gsva(param=gsvaParameter, verbose=FALSE)

## Calculate standard deviation for each sample using the permutation method
permResult <- splitTypeR:::permuteGSVA(geneLists=geneLists, 
    countMatrix=expNormalCountsDemo, permRatio=0.75, permNbr=20)

## For each sample, randomly select 10 values (nbValues) from the normal 
## curve where mean is the real GSVA value, and the standard deviation is 
## calculated from the permutation step.
normResult <- splitTypeR:::extractFromNormalDist(geneLists=geneLists, 
    gsvaRes=resClass, gsvaSD=permResult$SD, nbValues=10)

## Extracting the mixtures of two normal distributions for each signature
model <- splitTypeR:::normalMix(geneLists=geneLists, resultNorm=normResult)

## The two means of the normal distributions for the basal signature
model[["basal"]]$mu
#> [1] -0.5352405  0.3578356
